document_check.note: Document is Odusami M, Maskeliunas R, Damasevicius R. 'An Intelligent System for Early Recognition of Alzheimer's Disease Using Neuroimaging', Sensors 2022;22:740. It reports 98.86% accuracy for five-way AD/CN/EMCI/LMCI/MCI classification: matches the cited context.

cited_result: Five-way (AD, CN, EMCI, LMCI, MCI) slice-level classification by concatenated ResNet18/DenseNet121 features with Kaiming initialisation: test accuracy 98.86%.
tool_reason: The cited result is the accuracy of a deep-learning diagnostic classifier, so PROBAST with the PROBAST+AI considerations applies.

domains.rationale: This is a small convenience benchmark subset of ADNI sampled by diagnostic class, with 13 to 25 scans per class. No eligibility criteria are given, the SMC class is dropped without explanation, and the paper contradicts itself on the sample (138 scans with 13 MCI, versus 25 subjects per class and 125 in total).

signalling.question: 1.1 Were appropriate data sources used?
signalling.quote: There are 138 MRI scans in the dataset, with 25 CN, 25 SMC, 25 EMCI, 25 LMCI, 13 MCI, and 25 AD scans [18].

signalling.question: 1.2 Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
signalling.quote: where 25 subjects were used from each of the five categories of AD, MCI, EMCI, LMCI, and NC (a total of 125 subjects)

domains.rationale: The paper does not say how the 7509 images were derived from 138 scans: slice selection, plane and preprocessing are all missing. The modality is also ambiguous; the abstract refers to functional brain networks and the acknowledgements to fMRI. Blinding of slice selection to class cannot be judged.

signalling.quote: A total of 7509 processed MRI images were evaluated from the ADNI database

signalling.question: 2.2 Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
signalling.quote: Searched for slice selection, plane, preprocessing or registration steps: only 'processed MRI images' and resizing ('The images of the dataset were resized to 224 × 224 pixels') are reported.

signalling.question: 2.3 Are all predictors available at the time the model is intended to be used?
signalling.quote: The hospital server retrieves the patient’s brain MRI images from the MRI server, which are stored in NIfTI

domains.rationale: Class labels are said to come from cognitive test results, but no criteria are given for CN, EMCI, LMCI, MCI or AD. It is not explained what the 'MCI' class is, as distinct from EMCI and LMCI. The statement that every participant was diagnosed with AD contradicts the CN group.

signalling.quote: assigned to one of these phases according to their cognitive test results [18]

signalling.question: 3.6 Was the time interval between predictor assessment and outcome determination appropriate?

domains.rationale: There are very few participants per class. Train and validation images were split at random at image level, so slices from the same scan fall on both sides. The test set is tiny ('samples from one subject', 20 slices per class) and was used to choose the weight initialisation. The analysis ignores clustering of slices within participants, gives no confidence intervals or calibration, and reports figures inconsistently (the Discussion's accuracies differ from Table 4).

applicability.rationale: A tiny ADNI benchmark subset sampled by diagnostic class; not a clinical population.
Modality (structural MRI or fMRI) and slice selection are not clearly described.
The five-way labels include an undefined 'MCI' class separate from EMCI and LMCI, so the staging target does not correspond to a defined clinical construct.

overall_rationale: Domains 1 and 4 are high, and domains 2 and 3 are unclear. The design is a small diagnostic-class convenience sample with an image-level random split. The test set is tiny and was also used for model selection. There is no clustering adjustment, uncertainty or calibration, and the reporting is internally inconsistent.
